takeaways: Content that appears on hover or keyboard focus, such as tooltips, popovers and hover menus, must be dismissible, hoverable and persistent.
Dismissible: people can close it without moving the pointer or focus, usually with Esc. Hoverable: if hover opened it, the pointer can move onto it without it vanishing.
Persistent: it stays until hover or focus moves away, the person dismisses it, or its information is no longer valid. No timeouts.
Exception: content the browser controls, like the native title tooltip. Content opened by a click is not covered.
failures: A tooltip that disappears when the pointer moves toward it
A hover card that covers the next field and cannot be closed
A popover that fades out after a few seconds
check: Hover each trigger, then move the pointer onto the content. Does it stay?
Focus each trigger with the keyboard and press Esc. Does the content close and focus stay put?
Wait. Does anything disappear on its own?

quiz.question: A help tooltip appears on hover and covers the field below it. What must it support?
options: A close button inside the tooltip, and nothing else
Esc to close it, and staying open while the pointer moves onto it
quiz.why: A timeout breaks persistence, and a close button means moving the pointer, which may close it anyway. Esc closes it in place, and hoverability lets magnifier users read it.

spec: For each hover or focus reveal, specify the trigger, how it closes and that Esc dismisses it.
Show the hover bridge: no gap between trigger and content that closes it.
State that it has no timeout.
review: Can someone zoomed in to 400% move onto this tooltip and read it?
How do I get rid of this without moving my mouse?
Should this be on click instead of hover?
tradeoff: Hover reveals keep screens clean, but they are fragile. Keep essential information visible, and use hover and focus only for extras that follow these three rules.
system: Build one tooltip and one popover component with Esc dismissal, hoverability and no timeout, and ban custom hover reveals outside them.
pitch: People who magnify the screen see one small piece at a time. A tooltip that vanishes when they move toward it is help they can never read.
